title: Curriculum-Easy LR Sweep
subtitle: Three learning-rate arms RL-training the same 30B MoE instruct model on real terminal-agent tasks in Daytona sandboxes, racing to step 50. How each arm is trending, what every metric means, and what actually happened to all those Slurm jobs.
status_line: 3 arms alive — baseline 40/50, both sweep arms 20/50

charts.title: Training reward by step
charts.how: Each line = the share of terminal tasks completed on that step's training batch. Up and to the right would be learning; 40 steps in, nothing here clears the noise floor. The two dips to exactly 0.00 are **not** collapses — they are thin-batch steps, see the last chart. Hover or focus + arrow keys for exact values.

charts.title: Entropy — is anyone collapsing?
charts.how: Token-level hesitation. Drifting down = converging (fine). Crashing toward ~0.01 = mode collapse, the kill criterion. All three arms sit flat near 0.16 — nobody is collapsing.

charts.title: KL to reference — how far from base?
charts.how: Drift from the frozen starting model, held back by the KL penalty. **This is the one chart where the learning-rate lever is unmistakably working**: at step 20, lr5e6 has drifted about 7x further than lr1e6, in clean rank order. Reward has not followed.

charts.title: Answer length (median tokens)
charts.how: Median tokens per sampled answer. Watch for runaway growth (rambling) or a crash toward zero (degenerate short outputs). Steady in the 1,300–2,600 band throughout — neither pathology is present.

charts.title: Mixed groups — is there signal left?
charts.how: Share of tasks where the 8 rollouts disagree — the only place GRPO gradient comes from. Hovering near 0.25 means roughly three quarters of every batch is doing no work.

charts.title: Effective batch — how many samples actually counted
charts.how: The nominal batch is 128 samples (16 tasks × 8 rollouts). The async trainer discards rollouts generated against a stale policy, and at the first step after a checkpoint resume that can cut almost everything — 12 of the 13 post-resume steps ran short, twice down to a single group of 8. Read every dip on the reward chart against this line first.

explainer.title: What is this experiment?
paragraphs: Unlike the GSM8K campaign that validated the stack, this one is a **research** run: the model is graded on whether it actually completes a terminal task — it drives a shell inside a Daytona sandbox under the Terminus-2 harness, and the reward is binary (task done / not done) on the `tasktrove_curriculum_easy_rl511` task set.

All three arms are **identical except one lever**: the learning rate (1e-6 / 3e-6 / 5e-6). Same seed, same data, same 6 GH200 nodes, same 8 rollouts per task — so any daylight between the curves is caused by that one lever. The 3e-6 baseline arm started a day earlier and is correspondingly further along; compare arms **at equal step**, never at the right-hand edge.

Read the reward curve with care. Each point is at most 128 binary rollouts, so its noise floor is around **±0.04** even when nothing is changing, and step-to-step swings of 0.2 are routine. Forty steps in, the baseline is flat — 0.37 across its first five steps, 0.32 across its last five. The honest current answer is *no separation yet on reward*, not *it works* and not *it fails*. The one place the learning rate visibly bites is KL drift.

timeline.title: The job war — every Slurm attempt, Aug 16 04:00 → now
timeline.how: Each bar is one Slurm job; the dot at its end is how it died. Two enemies dominate. **Ghost-GPU OOM:** a node is returned to the pool before the previous job's GPU memory is actually released, so ours lands on a card already holding 60–85 GB of someone else's residue and dies at model load, checkpoint load, or the first backward peak. **EP/FSDP2 backward hang:** a known collective deadlock in expert-parallel backward. It cannot self-abort — blocking-wait mode is memory-load-bearing on 30B EP/FSDP2, so the NCCL watchdog is deliberately defanged and an external stall-watcher plus a human scancel is the detection layer. That is why every hang shows up in Slurm as CANCELLED rather than FAILED. The defense is the same either way: checkpoint every 5 steps, resume, exclude the crime scene, relaunch. Nothing but the steps since the last checkpoint was ever lost.

notes.text: Metrics come from the trainer's own WandB runs, which log **offline** on Jupiter — one run per Slurm attempt, under each experiment dir. They are rsynced off the cluster and `wandb sync`ed into lukeleeai/jupiter-currease30b-grpo, then stitched per arm latest-attempt-wins per step. Nothing here updates on its own: every refresh is a manual sync (`scripts/dashboard/refresh_currease.sh`). Job IDs, nodes and windows are read from each attempt's wandb-metadata.json and from sacct; fates are cross-checked against the operator incident ledger and the driver logs.

The async trainer discards rollouts generated against a stale policy. At the first step after a checkpoint resume that bites hard: **12 of the 13 post-resume steps ran on less than the nominal 128 samples**, twice collapsing to a single group of 8. Both of the reward curve's dips to exactly 0.00 (lr1e6 step 16, lr5e6 step 11) are those 8-sample steps — one group of eight rollouts all failing, which is a coin-flip event, not a policy collapse. With 39 restarts behind these curves, a good share of the visible jitter is batch size, not learning. Check the effective-batch chart before reading anything into a spike.

Reward is binary task completion averaged over the batch, so it is far noisier step-to-step than a math-accuracy curve — a single step's wobble means nothing. The metric to watch is **frac_groups_mixed**: only tasks where some of the 8 rollouts succeeded and some failed produce any gradient under GRPO. All-wrong and all-correct groups contribute exactly zero, and they remain about three quarters of every batch.

notes.lead: Where the LR lever actually shows.
notes.text: Reward is flat on all three arms, but **KL drift separates them cleanly and in rank order**: at step 20, lr1e6 sits at 0.0025 (essentially unmoved from the reference), lr3e6 at 0.0035, lr5e6 at 0.0177 — a 7x spread. lr5e6's entropy also runs slightly below the others. So the arms genuinely are different policies by now; that difference simply has not reached task completion. If reward is still flat at step 50 while KL keeps climbing, the honest read is that this task set is not teachable at this scale in 50 steps, not that the learning rate was wrong.

Truncation is **zero** on every arm — no rollout is hitting the 32k context wall — the TIS importance ratio sits at 1.000, and no arm's entropy is collapsing. The gaps in grad-norm are async steps where a partial batch was discarded, the same events as the thin-batch chart.
